claims.text: Conventional casting of CoCrFeNiTi yields a porous, soft, single-phase FCC structure.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi powder mixture has high oxygen content.
High-energy ball milling followed by SPS will suppress porosity in CoCrFeNiTi.
SPS at 1100–1200 °C, above 100 °C/min, with a 5–10 min dwell will kinetically retain a nanocrystalline solid solution.
The retained solid solution will be dominated by FCC with a minor BCC fraction.
Rapid sintering will prevent decomposition into a brittle Ti-rich HCP phase.
The proposed rapid SPS schedule will avoid excessive Cr/Ti-rich Laves-phase precipitation.
Maintaining the strain rate below an unspecified threshold will prevent thermal runaway during sintering.
The proposed process will produce grains smaller than 100 nm.
Solute drag from Ti and Cr will suppress grain growth.
Rapid solidification kinetics during the proposed SPS process will suppress grain growth and phase nucleation.
Rapid heating and short dwell times inhibit diffusion-controlled decomposition of FCC into HCP or Laves phases.
Defects introduced by high-energy milling lower the activation energy for FCC nucleation.
Rapid cooling prevents the formation of brittle intermetallics found in slowly cooled Ti-rich systems.
The processed alloy will be dense and porosity-free.
The processed alloy will exceed 400 HV and be significantly harder than cast material because of grain refinement.
Keeping the sintering temperature at or below 1250 °C will avoid Laves-phase precipitation.
In CoCrFeMnNi, HCP is relatively favored at low temperature and FCC reappears above approximately 633 K at ambient pressure.
The approximately 633 K HCP/FCC behavior of CoCrFeMnNi can be adapted to define an HCP stability window in Ti-rich CoCrFeNiTi.
A hardness comparison between the rapid and slow sintering schedules can distinguish grain-refinement strengthening from solute strengthening.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as solid-state milling plus SPS, but the proposed mediator invokes rapid solidification and rapid-solidification kinetics. No melting step is specified, so this mechanism is inconsistent with the stated solid-state route.

The operating range includes 1200 °C and is said to avoid Laves precipitation, while the boundary cites Laves precipitation in CrMoNbWV at 1200 °C as the rationale for a 1250 °C upper limit. The cited observation does not support that cutoff and conflicts with the claimed safe range.
The predicted outcome states that the alloy will be porosity-free, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that residual porosity may remain if pressure is insufficient.
